title: How a 70-Ton Messi Statue Turned a Remote Patagonian Oil Town Into a Football Pilgrimage Site
excerpt: Cutral Co, a town of 40,000 in Argentina's Neuquén province, has seen a surge of visitors since unveiling the world's tallest Messi monument during the 2026 World Cup.
body:
On the outskirts of Cutral Co, a town of roughly 40,000 people in Argentina's Neuquén province, motorists along National Route 22 now encounter something unexpected: a 26-metre-tall figure of Lionel Messi, kneeling with the 2022 World Cup trophy between his legs and one arm raised toward the sky.

The statue — built from 70 tons of steel and iron — was inaugurated on June 16, the day Argentina opened their 2026 World Cup campaign with a victory over Algeria. It has since turned a quiet oil town that rarely featured on tourist maps into one of Argentina's most talked-about new destinations.

From Oil Fields to Football Shrine

Cutral Co sits in the Patagonian steppe, far from the picturesque lakes and mountains that draw visitors to nearby Bariloche. Most families here work in the oil fields of Vaca Muerta, a formation holding some of the world's largest shale gas and oil reserves.

Beroisa, 61, is a local artist known for designing giant dinosaur sculptures and monuments to Argentina's independence heroes. He spent 18 months constructing the Messi tribute with help from local workers. The statue captures the moment at Lusail Stadium in Qatar when Gonzalo Montiel sealed Argentina's 4-2 penalty shootout victory over France — Messi falling to his knees, clutching his jersey, and pointing skyward in tribute to his late grandmother.

Local authorities declared it the tallest monument ever dedicated to the Argentine captain, surpassing a previous sculpture erected in Kolkata, India.

"He is Argentina's natural ambassador. For me, it was very important, not only as an artist but as an Argentine."

— Aldo Beroisa, sculptor, speaking to The Associated Press

A Gathering Point During the World Cup

What began as a roadside attraction quickly became a communal rallying point. During Argentina's semifinal against England on July 15, about 300 locals gathered around the statue to watch the match on a screen set up next to Messi's towering knees, Reuters reported. When the referee blew the final whistle after Argentina's 2-1 comeback, the crowd erupted.

The scene mirrored celebrations across Buenos Aires, where Argentina's run through the tournament has reignited the passion of 2022. Local newspapers have interviewed cardiologists warning about stress-related heart attacks as fans endure close calls and comeback victories.

Part of a Broader Messi Pilgrimage Circuit

The Cutral Co statue is part of a wider wave of Messi tributes during the 2026 tournament. In Berazategui, a suburb of Buenos Aires, artist Leonel García completed a hyperrealistic mural of Messi surrounded by the names of more than 1,300 supporters. The work caught Messi's attention.

"Crazy ... thank you very much to all of you, to the people who supported it, who came by, and who keep coming by," Messi said in a video message to the creators.

"When the referee blew the final whistle after Argentina's 2-1 comeback, the crowd erupted.</p> <blockquote class="pull-quote"> <p>"It was a victory of suffering."

For travellers, the statue joins a growing list of Messi-related landmarks. His hometown of Rosario has long attracted football tourists to the Newell's Old Boys stadium where he trained as a child. The Buenos Aires neighbourhood of La Boca, home to Boca Juniors' Bombonera, remains a staple on Argentine itineraries.
image_caption: The 85-foot Cutral Co Messi Statue stands along National Route 22 in Patagonia, Argentina. The 70-ton steel monument, created by sculptor Aldo Beroisa, was inaugurated during the 2026 World Cup.
